title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 785-786). A topological group G acts continuously on a surface X, and I (also written S) is a finite set of marked points fixed by G. For each x in I, D_x* is a punctured disc neighbourhood of x and D_x*~ is its universal cover. The group G~ (written both G~ and Ĝ on this page) consists of pairs (u, ũ): u is in G, and ũ is a family of lifts of u to the D_x*~. It sits in the extension (128), 1 -> ∏_x T_x -> G~ -> G -> 1, where T_x is the deck group of D_x*~, which is isomorphic to Z.

The problem on this page is to put a topology on G~. By continuity of the action there are disc neighbourhoods Δ_{x,1} ⊂ Δ_{x,0} of x and a neighbourhood U of 1 in G with U·Δ_{x,1} ⊂ Δ_{x,0}. For u in U, a lift ũ amounts to a lift ũ_{0,1}: Δ*~_{x,1} -> Δ*~_{x,0} compatible with u restricted to the punctured disc.

Let Ũ be the preimage of U in G~. Give Ũ the coarsest topology making three maps continuous (formula 134):
- p_1: Ũ -> U, the projection;
- q: (u, ũ) ↦ ũ_{0,1}, with values in Cont(Δ*~_{x,1}, Δ*~_{x,0}), presumably with the compact-open topology;
- q' = q∘σ, where σ is inversion, to control inverses.
One may take U symmetric, and then Ũ is symmetric too.

The neighbourhood filter of the identity in Ũ, pushed into G~, should be the neighbourhood filter of 1 for a group topology on G~. For that topology, G~ -> G should be a covering, i.e. a topological extension with discrete kernel ∏ T_x. Grothendieck does not check the axioms: 'J'admets que tout marche.'

He then specialises. Let X be an oriented connected surface and T its group of orientations; then each T_x is canonically isomorphic to T, which is isomorphic to Z. The extension becomes 1 -> T^I -> G~ -> G -> 1.

The universal case is G = Aut^+(X,S), the orientation-preserving homeomorphisms, with the topology of uniform convergence of u and u^{-1}. In the anabelian range 2g-2+ν > 0, the identity component A^0 is contractible. The extension therefore descends to an extension of the Teichmüller (mapping class) group, 1 -> Z^I -> T~ -> T(X,S) -> 1. In modern terms this is the mapping class group of the surface with the punctures replaced by boundary circles: the boundary Dehn twists form the kernel, and the extension is central.

The purpose is to build, inside the Longue Marche framework, the Teichmüller groups with 'tangential' structure at the punctures, the ones that carry the local inertia generators.
errors: No real error, but there is an acknowledged gap: Grothendieck explicitly admits, without proof, that the filter defines a group topology and that G~ -> G is a covering ('J'admets que tout marche').

Two details are left implicit. First, which topology Cont(-,-) carries (presumably compact-open). Second, that the construction does not depend on the choice of Δ_{x,0}, Δ_{x,1} and U. The 'covering' notion for a non-locally-compact homeomorphism group needs care; it is best read as a topological extension with discrete kernel.
On the next page, the contractibility of A^0 is invoked as known (Earle–Eells / Hamstrom type results). This is correct in the stated anabelian range.

ideas.what: Topologising the group of pairs (homeomorphism, lift to the universal covers of punctured disc neighbourhoods), via the initial topology for projection, local lift and lift of inverse, to get a topological extension of G by ∏ T_x
ideas.modern_name: Topological central extension of Homeo^+(X,S) by Z^S (lifts at punctures, analogous to the universal cover of Homeo^+(S^1))
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; analogous constructions for Homeo(S^1)~ go back to Poincaré rotation numbers and later work on Euler class / bounded cohomology

ideas.what: Descending the extension to the mapping class group via contractibility of Homeo_0 in the anabelian range: 1 -> Z^I -> T~ -> T(X,S) -> 1
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group of surface with boundary as central extension of punctured mapping class group by boundary Dehn twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Birman, and others; see Farb–Margalit, capping/boundary twist sequence)
ideas.where_published: Teichmüller groups with tangential/infinitesimal structure at points are alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche; this exact construction is not known to me in published form

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine (and admittedly unchecked) topologisation leading to the well-known boundary-twist central extension of the mapping class group. It is interesting only as documentation of how Grothendieck built 'tangential' Teichmüller groups from homeomorphism groups.
transcription_corrections: 'On aurait pu soin de prendre' should read 'On aurait pu avoir soin de prendre 𝒰 stable par u ↦ u^{-1}'.
In (134) 'induite par Ĝ → G': both Ĝ and G~ notations occur for the same extension group; '$\tilde{\hat G}$' should simply be Ĝ (= G~).
'et que ... est un rev. de G' reads roughly 'Ĝ → G top., et que [pour celle-ci Ĝ] est un rev. de G'; the struck words are 'des groupes', followed by 'J'admets que tout marche'.
The last line reads 'Quand X est une surface orientable, connexe, et si T désigne son module des orientations' (continuing on p. 786); 'une surface' is inserted above the struck 'compacte'.
In the q line, the struck alternative is '(u,ũ) ↦ (ũ^{-1})_{0,1}', replaced by ũ_{0,1}.
